steps.why: The mark is for the contrast with the artificial system: many characters together instead of one selected character.
common_mistakes: Saying it uses evolutionary relationship. That is the phylogenetic system.
Saying it uses only one character. That is the artificial system.
steps.memory_tip: Artificial = one character. Natural = many characters. Phylogenetic = descent.
steps.margin_note: Two lines. Say "all important characters, mostly morphological".

steps.label: The scientists

lines.text: George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker

lines: They set it out in their book Genera Plantarum.
It is the best known natural system, and
herbaria still arrange their specimens by it.
steps.why: The question asks for names, so the two names and their book are the whole second mark.
common_mistakes: Spelling it Bantham. The book prints that misspelling; the correct name is Bentham.
Naming Linnaeus. His sexual system is the artificial system.
steps.memory_tip: Bentham and Hooker wrote Genera Plantarum: two men, one book, the natural system.
steps.margin_note: Write both full names. Adding the book name is safe and costs one line.

insider_note: Examiners accept "Bentham and Hooker" alone, but the book name Genera Plantarum makes the answer look certain.
